claims.text: Deep cryogenic treatment can be applied as post-processing to laser-melting-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr high-entropy-alloy parts.
The Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy considered has a BCC structure.
As-manufactured LMD components exhibit fabrication-induced defects.
As-manufactured LMD components exhibit dimensional imprecision.
DCT induces a phase transition in the LMD Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy without additional deformation.
DCT relieves residual internal stresses in the additively manufactured alloy.
The DCT-induced microstructural reconfiguration reduces defect density.
The DCT-induced microstructural reconfiguration improves dimensional precision.
DCT improves the strength-ductility combination of LMD Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr.
After DCT, the alloy's tensile strength is about 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy.
After DCT, the alloy's tensile strength is higher than that of the untreated as-deposited alloy.
After DCT, the alloy's ductility is higher than that of the untreated as-deposited alloy.
DCT improves the dimensional accuracy of LMD HEA parts relative to untreated as-deposited parts.
DCT reduces residual fabrication-induced defects relative to untreated as-deposited parts.
The expected effects may not generalize to alloys with different crystal structures or additive-manufacturing thermal histories.
The quantitative effect of DCT on dimensional precision in additively manufactured parts is less established than its effect on strength and ductility.

The hypothesis can be tested by comparing otherwise identically manufactured DCT-treated and untreated LMD samples using dimensional metrology, microscopy, tensile testing, and residual-stress measurements.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in dimensional accuracy, defect density, tensile strength, and ductility, or degradation of any property, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The quantified 25% tensile-strength improvement uses an as-cast comparator, whereas the declared experimental baseline is untreated as-deposited LMD material. The cited evidence gives the improvement against the as-deposited baseline as 11%, not 25%.
